title: perf(canary): adaptive auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Our current perf canary detects regressions using fixed thresholds which require frequent manual tuning and produce noisy flips during traffic spikes. This PR introduces an adaptive auto-detection algorithm for latency and throughput regressions, plus rollout guard integration to prevent bad canary rollouts. Scope: 1) Adaptive detector service that learns baseline distributions per-model/route and applies hysteresis and confidence-weighted thresholds. 2) KV-cache-aware heuristics to avoid false positives when cold cache events spike latency. 3) Rollout guard policies that can block/rollback canaries based on multi-metric signals (p95 latency, tail latency, throughput drop, error-rate increase) and confidence intervals. 4) Backwards-compatible config: default behavior preserves existing thresholds; teams can opt-in via canary.policy.type=adaptive. 5) Tests and perf-e2e harness updates, docs, and migration guide. This is targeted at improving signal-to-noise for perf canaries and reducing unnecessary rollbacks while catching real regressions earlier.

review_thread: Ravi Patel: This looks promising — can you explain how the detector handles low-volume routes? Risk of overfitting?

Ava Martinez: For low-volume routes we fall back to a longer bootstrap window and increase the confidence threshold; this is configurable per-route. Added notes in docs and unit tests to cover low-volume behaviour.
Morgan Lee: We should ensure rollout guards don't mistakenly block canaries during infra incidents (region outage). How does region-level anomalies affect decisions?

Ava Martinez: Rollout guard supports scope-scoped signals; we use region-scoped metric aggregation by default and expose a "scope" parameter so teams can restrict evaluation to global/region/zone. Also added an option to pause detection when global infra-alert is present.
Elena Rossi: CI showed an intermittent failure in test_policy_engine.test_rollback_on_multi_metric_regression — I saw a race in the test harness. Please stabilize.
Ava Martinez: Fixed the race by adding deterministic time advancement in the test harness and increased retry window. Re-ran tests locally and on CI.
Ravi Patel: Approving after a couple nits on naming (see inline).

release_notes: Introduce adaptive perf canary detector (opt-in). Adds hysteresis and confidence-weighted thresholds, KV-cache-aware heuristics to reduce false positives, and rollout guard policies that can block/rollback canaries based on multi-metric signals. Backwards-compatible flags available in defaults.yaml. See docs/perf-canary/adaptive-detector.md for migration steps.
upgrade_guide: 1) Default behaviour remains unchanged. 2) To opt-in, set canary.policy.type=adaptive in your canary config. 3) Tune canary.policy.adaptive.bootstrap_window and confidence_threshold for low-volume routes. 4) If using Private deployment, ensure metrics agent emits cache_state tag. 5) Run the provided perf-harness canary_burst scenario before enabling in prod.
risk_assessment: Medium. Algorithm is opt-in and defaults preserve existing behaviour. Main risks: misconfiguration on low-volume routes and interactions with infra incidents. Mitigations: defaults tuned for conservative detection, tests, and an explicit pause-on-infra-alert option.
observability_changes: New metrics: perf_canary.detector.confidence, perf_canary.detector.baseline_p95, perf_canary.policy.evaluation_latency. Added trace tags: canary_id, cache_state, detector_confidence. Dashboard: perf-canary/adaptive-detector overview (draft).
migration_notes: No forced migration. Teams should opt-in per-canary. Docs include recommended defaults and recipes for common workloads.
merge_outcome: Squash merged by Ava Martinez after approvals. No follow-up rollbacks required. Deployed to staging and promoted to canary cluster; monitoring alerts configured to watch new detector confidence metric.
